tasks.title: Migrate both bridge taxonomies and consumer bindings
tasks.goal: Change the two bridge wrappers to flow at their accepted 1.0.0 while preserving package and upstream identities.
steps: Bind isolated writable external checkouts; record before-captures, wrapper coordinates/version, kind and upstream pins.
Change only wrapper kind/capability declarations needed for flow and own wrapper contracts; retain accepted 1.0.0 and all upstream attribution/versions.
Create consumer old→new kind/capability fixtures using the accepted migration machinery; identify every changed lock/manifest field instead of silently reselecting.
positive_cases: Both wrappers are flow at 1.0.0 with unchanged upstream provenance.
A consumer migrates its authored binding and lock deterministically.
negative_cases: No upstream release number or capture bytes are relabeled as Vibe-owned.
No new version bump or public publication is inferred from the kind change.
acceptance: Exact isolated external diffs show only intended wrapper/migration changes.
Consumer fixture preserves selected behavior and source identity.
tasks.safe_stop: Local external diffs and consumer migration evidence are ready; no publication.
tasks.commit_subject: feat(bridges): migrate wrapper kinds to flow at 1.0.0
notes: External logical roots are unbound authoring metadata. Before execution, the root must provide isolated checkouts for external:org.speckit.speckit and/or external:com.external-skills.skills and verify their exact captures. Never write the currently existing sibling source trees. External package checks are taken from that checkout's own declared commands; no unverified command is claimed here.

tasks.title: Preserve complete foreign resources and source interpretation
tasks.goal: Deliver each bridge's complete captured resources without treating imported content as Vibe specifications.
steps: Apply M-06-A classification to imported CommonMark/XML-data/opaque content; keep authored Vibe wrappers separately declared.
Project the audited closure, including nested templates/scripts/data/notices, with exact captured bytes and path layout.
Use prepared offline fixtures to validate file membership, duplicate-name interpretations and resource export compatibility; fix demonstrated projection loss in its owning engine.
positive_cases: Nested resources and notices survive preparation/projection byte-for-byte.
Foreign Vibe-looking markers remain inert; ordinary same-stem files coexist by identity.
negative_cases: No XML-data reserialization or automatic script execution occurs.
acceptance: Both bridges have complete resource manifests and byte-verified offline projections.
Source classification is shared rather than a bridge-local suffix workaround.
tasks.safe_stop: Foreign resource projection works in isolated fixtures; no publisher invoked.
